senate.title: Eliminate the legislative filibuster
senate.what: Changes Senate rules so most bills can pass with a simple majority instead of 60 votes, which would let a Democratic majority move much of this agenda without Republican support.

senate.title: Re-elect Chuck Schumer as Democratic leader
senate.what: Decides whether Chuck Schumer stays as leader of the Senate Democratic caucus, which shapes who sets the floor schedule and the party's strategy for the next two years.

senate.title: Medicare for All Act
senate.what: Replaces private insurance with a single public plan covering every American, ending premiums and deductibles but requiring large new federal taxes to pay for it.

senate.title: Restore the enhanced ACA premium tax credits
senate.what: Brings back the larger ACA marketplace subsidies that expired after 2025, lowering premiums for millions of people who buy their own coverage.

senate.title: Repeal the OBBBA Medicaid cuts and work requirements
senate.what: Reverses the Medicaid funding cuts and new work requirements in the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act, keeping coverage for people projected to lose it.

senate.title: Expand Medicare drug price negotiation (SMART Prices Act)
senate.what: Lets Medicare negotiate prices on many more drugs each year, which would lower costs for seniors and federal spending on prescriptions.

senate.title: Curb prior authorization (Improving Seniors' Timely Access to Care Act)
senate.what: Requires Medicare Advantage plans to approve routine care faster through electronic prior authorization, cutting delays for patients and paperwork for doctors.

senate.title: Codify Roe: the Women's Health Protection Act
senate.what: Creates a federal right to provide and receive abortion care, overriding most state bans and restrictions passed since Roe v. Wade was overturned.

senate.title: Ban grocery price-gouging and limit surveillance pricing
senate.what: Makes excessive grocery price hikes illegal and limits stores' use of personal data to charge different shoppers different prices.

senate.title: Break up meatpackers (Family Grocery and Farmer Relief Act) and block grocery mergers
senate.what: Forces the biggest meatpackers to sell off lines of business and blocks new grocery mergers, aiming to restore competition and lower meat prices.

senate.title: Suspend the federal gas tax
senate.what: Temporarily stops the 18.4-cent-per-gallon federal gas tax, giving drivers a modest break at the pump at the cost of highway funding.

senate.title: Make data centers pay their own power costs and cap utility hikes
senate.what: Requires data centers to cover the full cost of the power and grid upgrades they need and limits utility rate increases, so households aren't left paying for the AI boom.

senate.title: Expand the Child Tax Credit
senate.what: Makes the Child Tax Credit larger and available in full to low-income families, which cut child poverty sharply when it was temporarily expanded in 2021.

senate.title: Cap child care at 7% of income / universal child care
senate.what: Caps what families pay for child care at 7% of their income and funds more providers, moving toward child care that every family can afford.

senate.title: Repeal the OBBBA top-bracket cuts and close billionaire loopholes
senate.what: Undoes the 2025 tax cuts for the highest earners and closes loopholes used by billionaires, raising revenue for other priorities.

senate.title: National paid family and medical leave
senate.what: Guarantees workers paid time off to care for a new child, a sick relative or their own illness, funded through a national insurance program.

senate.title: ROAD to Housing Act (housing supply and permitting)
senate.what: Speeds up permitting and funds new construction to increase the housing supply, aiming to bring down rents and home prices over time.

senate.title: Down payment assistance for first-time buyers
senate.what: Gives first-time and first-generation homebuyers federal help with a down payment, making it easier for renters to buy a home.

senate.title: Raise the minimum wage ($15–$25) and expand overtime
senate.what: Raises the federal minimum wage from $7.25 to between $15 and $25 an hour and expands overtime pay, giving raises to millions of low-wage workers.

senate.title: PRO Act (Protecting the Right to Organize)
senate.what: Makes it easier for workers to form unions and bargain, and adds penalties for employers who illegally fight organizing drives.

senate.title: Federal right-to-repair for farm equipment
senate.what: Requires equipment makers to give farmers and independent shops the tools, parts and software needed to fix their own machines.

senate.title: Ban congressional stock trading: the Peters–Hawley–Merkley–Ossoff bill, covering the President and VP
senate.what: Bars members of Congress, the President and the Vice President from trading individual stocks while in office, removing a major conflict of interest.

senate.title: Ban partisan gerrymandering
senate.what: Bans partisan gerrymandering of congressional districts nationwide, so maps can't be drawn to lock in one party's advantage.

senate.title: DC and Puerto Rico statehood
senate.what: Admits Washington, DC and Puerto Rico as states, giving their residents full voting representation in Congress and adding four senators.

senate.title: Ban corporate PACs and super PACs
senate.what: Bans corporate PAC contributions and super PACs, cutting off the main channels for unlimited corporate and outside money in federal elections.

senate.title: Constitutional amendment for congressional term or age limits
senate.what: Amends the Constitution to cap how long members of Congress can serve, which needs two-thirds of both chambers and approval by 38 states.

senate.title: Comprehensive immigration reform
senate.what: Overhauls the immigration system by pairing border security with a path to legal status for long-time undocumented residents.

senate.title: Rein in ICE: no masks, body cameras, visible ID, judicial warrants, right to sue
senate.what: Sets new limits on immigration agents, including no masks, visible ID, body cameras, judicial warrants and the right to sue over abuses.

senate.title: Condition military aid to Israel
senate.what: Puts conditions on U.S. military aid to Israel, such as limits on offensive weapons, tied to how the weapons are used in Gaza.

senate.title: Iran War Powers Resolution
senate.what: Uses the War Powers Resolution to require congressional approval for continued U.S. military action against Iran.

senate.title: End the tariff emergencies and pass the Trade Review Act
senate.what: Ends the emergency declarations behind the current tariffs and requires Congress to approve new ones, which would lower import costs for businesses and shoppers.

senate.title: AI guardrails
senate.what: Sets federal safety and accountability rules for AI and keeps states free to pass their own protections.

governor.title: Expand Medicaid and raise provider rates
governor.what: Extends Medicaid to low-income adults in states that haven't expanded and raises payments to providers, adding coverage and helping rural hospitals stay open.

governor.title: A state board to negotiate prescription drug prices
governor.what: Creates a state board that can set upper payment limits on high-cost prescription drugs, lowering what patients and health plans pay.

governor.title: A state public health insurance option
governor.what: Offers a state-backed health plan anyone can buy, adding a lower-cost choice and competition in the individual insurance market.

governor.title: Cancel medical debt and keep it off credit reports
governor.what: Buys up and erases residents' medical debt and bars it from credit reports, so illness doesn't wreck people's ability to rent or borrow.

governor.title: End prior authorization and insulin co-pays
governor.what: Ends insurer pre-approval rules for routine care and caps or eliminates insulin co-pays, speeding treatment and cutting out-of-pocket costs.

governor.title: Backfill lost ACA subsidies with state money
governor.what: Uses state money to replace the federal ACA subsidies that expired after 2025, keeping marketplace premiums affordable.

governor.title: Make data centers pay their full costs
governor.what: Makes data centers pay their full power, water and grid costs and ends their tax breaks, so households don't subsidize them through higher bills.

governor.title: Utility accountability: caps on fees, limits on utility influence
governor.what: Caps utility fees and limits utilities' political spending and lobbying costs on customers' bills, giving regulators more power to hold down rates.

governor.title: Emergency rate freezes and bill credits
governor.what: Freezes utility rates or orders bill credits during an affordability emergency, giving households immediate relief on energy costs.

governor.title: Push regulators and the grid operator to cap prices
governor.what: Pushes state regulators and the regional grid operator to cap wholesale electricity prices, limiting how much power-market spikes reach customers' bills.

governor.title: Cut gas taxes or send direct payments
governor.what: Cuts or suspends the state gas tax, or sends households direct payments, to offset high fuel prices.

governor.title: Ease zoning and building rules, including statewide preemption
governor.what: Loosens zoning and building rules, sometimes overriding local limits, so more homes can be built and rents and prices can come down.

governor.title: Fast-track housing by executive action
governor.what: Uses executive orders and emergency powers to speed up permits and financing for housing already in the pipeline.

governor.title: Housing trust funds and bonds
governor.what: Creates dedicated funds or bonds that finance the construction of affordable homes and apartments.

governor.title: Down payment help and a broker-fee ban
governor.what: Gives first-time buyers help with down payments and bans renters from paying brokers' fees, lowering the upfront cost of a home or apartment.

governor.title: Renter protections
governor.what: Adds renter protections such as caps on security deposits and junk fees and bans on algorithmic rent-fixing.

governor.title: Limit corporate homebuying
governor.what: Limits how many single-family homes large investors can buy, leaving more starter homes for families.

governor.title: Pay for property-tax cuts by ending corporate giveaways
governor.what: Pays for homeowner property-tax cuts by ending tax breaks and subsidies for corporations.

governor.title: Targeted property-tax relief
governor.what: Targets property-tax relief at homeowners and seniors through larger exemptions, credits or rebates.

governor.title: Middle-class tax cuts
governor.what: Cuts state income taxes for middle-class families, for example through a bigger standard deduction or no tax on tips and overtime.

governor.title: State child and working-family tax credits
governor.what: Creates or expands a state child tax credit or earned income credit, putting cash directly into working families' pockets.

governor.title: End state tax on Social Security and seniors
governor.what: Stops taxing Social Security and other retirement income, lowering taxes for seniors.

governor.title: A millionaire's tax
governor.what: Adds a higher income tax rate on earnings above $1 million, raising revenue for housing, schools or other priorities.

governor.title: Universal pre-K
governor.what: Offers free pre-K to every four-year-old (and sometimes three-year-olds), helping kids start school ready and saving parents child care costs.

governor.title: Universal child care
governor.what: Builds a child care system every family can afford, often by capping costs as a share of income and funding providers directly.

governor.title: Raise teacher pay
governor.what: Raises teacher pay, such as a higher minimum starting salary, to recruit and keep teachers.

governor.title: Fund public schools fully instead of vouchers
governor.what: Opposes or repeals private-school voucher programs and puts that money into fully funding public schools.

governor.title: Paid family and medical leave
governor.what: Creates a state insurance program that gives workers paid time off for a new child, a sick relative or their own illness.

governor.title: $15 minimum wage
governor.what: Raises the state minimum wage to $15 an hour, giving raises to the lowest-paid workers.

governor.title: Write abortion rights into state law
governor.what: Writes the right to abortion into state law or the state constitution, protecting access regardless of federal action.

governor.title: Bar ICE from sensitive locations
governor.what: Bars immigration agents from schools, hospitals, courthouses and places of worship without a judicial warrant.

governor.title: Keep a federalized National Guard out of the state without the governor's consent
governor.what: Opposes the president federalizing the Guard or sending other states' troops into the state over the governor's objection, through lawsuits, refusals or state laws barring those deployments.

governor.title: National Popular Vote Interstate Compact
governor.what: Joins the interstate compact to award the state's electoral votes to the national popular-vote winner, which takes effect once states with 270 votes sign on.

governor.title: Automatic voter registration
governor.what: Registers eligible citizens to vote automatically when they deal with state agencies like the DMV, unless they opt out.

governor.title: Anti-fraud overhaul (audits, inspector general)
governor.what: Overhauls oversight of state programs with surprise audits and an independent inspector general to catch fraud and waste.
